CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports doing well. She has been taking prednisone 1 mg daily, which appears to be sufficient. She had a couple of days where she took an extra dose due to mild foot pain, occurring approximately once a week. Pain tends to worsen on days off when she is more active, as she has a desk job. She reports that methotrexate has been helpful for joint pain. She discontinued methotrexate for one week prior to her first COVID vaccine due to concerns about vaccine efficacy, during which time she felt "absolutely horrible" until restarting the medication one week later. She continued methotrexate with her second COVID vaccine dose after contacting a hotline. She reports easy bruising, particularly on her legs, which she does not feel when it occurs. She denies knowing the source of the bruises.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports joint pain in feet and knees, improved with increased methotrexate dosing. Easy bruising noted. Ridges in nails noted secondary to psoriasis.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily (to be discontinued).
Methotrexate (dose not specified in conversation).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works a desk job.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient ambulatory. Extremities: Mild tenderness in hand and foot joints. Good knee flexion range of motion. Good toe flexion with good range of motion. Ridges noted on nails consistent with psoriasis. No other significant findings noted on examination.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis: Well-controlled on current methotrexate regimen. Discontinue prednisone today. Continue methotrexate. Monitor for resolution of easy bruising with prednisone discontinuation. Patient to schedule blood work at front desk. Follow-up appointment in 3 months.
